newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends up on higher cash, outages.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends up on higher cash, outages.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended higher Thursday with strength from higher physicals prices and some power unit outages in the West, industry sources said.

California Oregon Border (COB) physicals prices were reported to have moved higher Thursday with some limited heating demand in the U.S. Northwest as cool temperatures were forecast to cover the region into October.

Several outages were also cited as putting some psychological pressure on futures, including the shutdown of Edison International's 790 megawatt Mohave coal-fired unit near Laughlin, Nevada, which was expected to resume production on Monday.
"Over the counter (power) looked very strong, and fundamentally people are just looking at this and comparing it with gas prices," one futures broker said.
November COB futures ended up 15 cents at $16.95 after trade as high as $17.05, while December settled up 12 cents at $18.27 from trade as high as $18.30 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Most remaining COB deferreds settled up five cents.
November Palo Verde (PV) closed up 40 cents at $15.95 from trade as high as $16.00, while December PV ended steady at $16.95 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds settled up strongly, between 20 and 50 cents, including August, 1997 which closed up 50 cents at $23.75 per MWh.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 245 COB and 207 PV contracts traded Thursday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
